name: inverter_dc_power
schreibeffekt: read-only (FC03); FC06/FC10 to < 40000 -> exception 2 (TCP_FC06_WriteSingle_Handler@0x080230d0, RS485 equivalent), Write_Handler is never reached
einheit_skala_A: W, x1, i16; + = power into the battery from the AC side (charging), - = power to the AC side (discharge/feed-in); PV share removed by the micro itself
ziel_A: Micro: A Micro 1211 telemetry block +0x1C: +0x1C i16 = (short)(g_batPowerFilteredW - g_mpptPowerW) (CAN_UpdateTelemetryPayload@0x08008a80). g_batPowerFilteredW 0x20100594 = 0.1*V_avg*I_avg + 0.9*previous, per grid period (Inv_StateMachine l.2852)
leseeffekt_A: W, x1, i16; + = power into the battery from the AC side (charging), - = power to the AC side (discharge/feed-in); PV share removed by the micro itself. Served as is (scale code 0; serializer sign bug does not apply).
befund_A: Sign convention as on D (discharge < 0). Difference: the A micro subtracts its own MPPT power, so the value is the AC-converter DC power, not the pack power. Sign evidence: Inv_StateMachine l.2097-2116 treats g_batPowerFilteredW >= 30 W at SoC 100 % as 'battery still charging' (off-grid frequency shift), i.e. + = charging; consistent with the a.yaml field note (-1557 W read while packs gave 870 W and PV 723 W). | Analysed on Control 1509 + Micro 1211; re-checked 2026-10-11 against Control 151 (no newer Micro image). Control read/CAN path code-identical to D 151 (diff of Telemetry_Register_Dispatcher, Protocol_AA_SetChannelData, Modbus_StoreRegisterSlot, Modbus_StoreWithHandshake, Energy_Stats_Accumulate_And_Save, Stats_Clear_Counters, CAN_Broadcast_Category0x16_PackedValues, ShellCmd_get_mppt_data: renamed variables only). | VERIFIED (V4): exact relation: battery_power = 30001 + 0.970 x (sum of PV powers - 8 W); the plain Suite sum 30001 + mppt1..4_power reads about 3 % of PV + 8 W too high.

The derived battery_power = 30001 + mppt1..4_power matches the code (the micro subtracts g_mpptPowerW, which is the sum of the running channels; the per-channel report powers are zeroed below 5 W, so small differences are expected).
